faq.q: Does the $800K cap cover the typical Mission condo?
faq.a: The cap sits above the middle of the combined attached market: the Mission Condos & Townhomes median sale price was $430,000 in September 2026 — $370,000 below the cap — though that median mixes townhomes with condos and swung from $642,500 in August 2026 on small sold counts, so treat it as context for where the cap sits, not as the price of a typical condo (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Where does Mission's attached stock actually sit?
faq.a: By September 2026 inventory, the urban "Mission" sub-area held 104 Condos & Townhomes listings, Mission West 8 and Hemlock 9, out of 122 Mission-wide, and the rural sub-areas held almost none — those are combined condo-and-townhome inventory counts, not counts of condos under the cap (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which school district serves Mission, and how are catchments set?
faq.a: SD75 Mission Public Schools; catchments are address-based — at the downtown sample address used here (7466 Welton St) the locator gives École Mission Central Elementary, Heritage Park Middle School and Mission Senior Secondary; SD75 runs a middle tier (Grades 7–9), and any specific condo address should be confirmed with SD75's School Locator Tool.

faq.q: What do strata fees cover on a condo in Mission?
faq.a: Strata fees pay for upkeep and insurance of the common property and the contingency reserve fund, and in some buildings heat, hot water or other services. The Form B Information Certificate lists exactly what a unit's fee covers.

faq.q: What should I read before buying a condo in Mission?
faq.a: The Form B, the bylaws, the last two years of strata minutes, the depreciation report and the contingency reserve fund balance. They show planned repairs, special levies and rules on pets and rentals.
